text:
Aisha: quick heads-up — after landing PTQ for the new reranker candidate (bert-lite-ptq), our nightly eval shows a ~3.8pt NDCG@10 drop on the internal news_holdout set but MRR is flat. anyone seen this pattern before?

Marco: interesting, same model family as previous runs? quant settings changed? :thinking_face:

Aisha: same family, only change was INT8 PTQ with per-channel activation calibration. quant config: `per_channel=true, calibration_samples=2048, clip=0.9999`

Riley: can you paste the eval summary? full numbers + slice breakdown pls

Aisha: pasted below (from EvalBot job 2026-05-12):
```
EvalBot: model=bert-lite-ptq
holdout=news_holdout
NDCG@10: baseline=0.712 -> ptq=0.674 (-0.038)
MRR@10: baseline=0.483 -> ptq=0.481 (-0.002)
slices: short-queries: -0.012, long-queries: -0.054, long-docs: -0.061
```

Sasha: long-docs slice hit the worst regression. Could be truncation / KV cache mismatch in serving vs eval runtime. Did we change doc-prep or tokenizer?

Aisha: dev branch used new doc-concat flow (concat with " \n\n" separator) vs prod used single-passage prep. Also the eval harness uses the HF tokenizer v2.1 whereas serve uses v2.0 (we pinned for latency).

Marco: tokenizer drift + different concat separator could explain NDCG drop for long docs — reranker is sensitive to passage boundaries. Suggest reproducing by running baseline & ptq through identical pipeline: same tokenizer version + same doc prep.

Riley: also check candidate ordering: were candidates shuffled before scoring? A previous regression we fixed looked like candidate-order bias when top-k was applied differently between sampling and eval harness.

Aisha: good call. I re-ran a quick smoke locally forcing HF v2.1 and original single-passage prep; numbers look much closer: NDCG diff down to -0.008 for that config.

EvalBot: rerun job queued (job id 98321). config: ptq, hf_tokenizer=2.1, doc_prep=single_passage, seed=42

Sasha: if that confirms, we should either revert doc-prep change or add a tokenizer-compatibility step to the PTQ onboarding checklist. Also add a slice-level regression alert for long-docs in the gauntlet.

Marco: forensics checklist: 1) reproduce with same tokenizer + prep (Aisha) 2) run per-slice attribution (Riley) 3) run candidate-order determinism test (Sasha) 4) sanity-check quant calibration samples (Marco)

Aisha: will run the reproduction now and share results in this thread. ETA ~45m.

Riley: quick note — when you paste logs, include the exact prompt formatting we sent to the reranker (we had an invisible leading space in one experiment that altered tokenization).

Aisha: noted. small update: reproduction job completed, NDCG delta -0.009 (much smaller). looks like tokenizer + doc-prep mismatch was the bulk. still seeing tiny residual on long-docs slice.

Marco: residual could be PTQ calibration instability. try increasing calibration_samples to 8k or use per-layer scale folding. Also capture logits for top-5 candidates to compare ranking score shifts.

Aisha: trying calibration_samples=8192 now. If that nudges long-docs slice back, we'll add a PTQ quality gate that requires long-doc slice not drop >0.01 NDCG.

EvalBot: job 98324 finished: calibration_samples=8192 -> NDCG delta -0.003, long-docs -0.008

Sasha: nice. proposed next steps: add tokenizer version pin in onboarding docs, add doc-prep compatibility test in gauntlet, and add PTQ gate for critical slices. I'll draft a short RFC and PR templates for the checks.

Aisha: thanks all. I'll open a PR to pin HF tokenizer in the eval infra and update the PTQ checklist with the new calibration threshold. cc @EvalBot for adding slice alerts. :thumbsup:

Marco: +1. if anyone wants the raw per-query diffs I exported a parquet to s3://redwood-evals/bugs/1719891234-diffs.parquet

Riley: can you also attach the top-5 logits dump? useful for future attribution

Marco: uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/bugs/1719891234-logits.jsonl

Aisha: closing loop — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-evals/pull/212. Thanks team, keeping this one as a learning case for PTQ-onboard playbook.
